answer: Anchor each agent identity to one autonomous system number with a signed RPKI route attestation. First the agent publishes its ASN and proof of control over its prefix. Then the registry rejects any ASN already tied to another identity. Next it answers a signed challenge inside its own block, proving control. A farm wanting 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 ASNs, each about $500 a year plus an IP block, so the attack burns $500,000 a year before it earns a cent. Stamped timber traces to one forest; karst caves cannot hide a missing registration, the kernel of trust is ground no one can photocopy.
